title: Example 18-5: Isolated Punctuation Is Emphasized

illustrates.quote: When isolated punctuation is emphasized with something other than italics, bold, underlining, or script, insert a transcriber’s note after the punctuation mark or applicable word to identify the print emphasis.

blocks.text: I didn’t think so, *but that’s it.*
blocks.features: Print (page-500.png): 'I didn’t think so, but that’s it.' with 'but that’s it.' in italics and the apostrophe of 'that’s' printed in red. The print shows no note.
not-representable: rule 18.3.3c has the transcriber insert a note after the red apostrophe; its wording and position are the transcriber's, not in the print.

print.notes: The print page (page-500.png) shows the sentence only; the transcriber's note is braille content and is not built.
print.printFeatures: The phrase "but that's it." is italicized; the apostrophe in "that's" is red.
